assessment.body:
## Verdict

agent_supports: yes
daemon_capability: full; driver_capability: ready

## Reasoning

The scenario asserts exactly two user-observable bullets: (1) the session row appears in `ready` within 1s of agent launch, and (2) the PID is bound within 1s. Both land inside the copilot adapter's observability surface, and — as with claudecode — both are carried by the daemon's pre-session row rather than by the transcript, because Copilot materializes its transcript lazily.

**Bullet 1 — ready within 1s.** `Agent()` in `core/adapters/inbound/agents/copilot/agent.go` declares `Process.Match = agent.ExactName{Name: ProcessName}` with `ProcessName = "copilot"`. The generic scanner (`core/adapters/inbound/agents/processlifecycle/scanner.go:347`, `:543`) mints a `proc-<PID>` pre-session row in `ready` on the first tick that sees the process, for every adapter that declares a matcher — nothing copilot-specific has to work for the row to exist. That row is therefore observable from launch, independent of any file on disk.

The real `<session-id>` row arrives later. Copilot creates `$COPILOT_HOME/session-state/<session-id>/` at launch, but that directory initially holds only `workspace.yaml`; `events.jsonl` is not written until the first user prompt (verified live on CLI 1.0.77). `sessionIDFromPath` in `adapter.go` deliberately accepts only the constant `events.jsonl` basename, so `workspace.yaml` cannot mint a premature row — the `<session-id>` session is born when the first prompt materializes the transcript. The recipe's one-token nudge is what makes that happen, exactly as claudecode's does.

The interesting risk for this adapter is whether the watcher sees a transcript inside a directory that did not exist when the watcher started — every real Copilot launch creates its session directory at runtime, so a watcher attached only to startup-present directories would observe nothing at all in production. `core/adapters/inbound/agents/copilot/watcher_test.go` (`TestWatcher_EmitsSessionForNewDirectory`) pins precisely that shape: it starts the watcher, waits for `Ready()`, then creates `<root>/<uuid>/events.jsonl` and asserts an event carrying the directory-derived session id.

Birth lands in `ready`, not `working`: `parseSessionStart` sets `ev.Skip = true`, so the `session.start` line cannot trip the classifier's default "transcript activity → working" rule while still supplying `cwd` and `copilotVersion` through the tailer's skipped-event metadata path.

**Bullet 2 — PID bound within 1s.** The `proc-<PID>` row is keyed by PID from inception, so binding happens on the same scanner tick as birth. For the `<session-id>` row, `DiscoverPID` (`pid.go`) delegates to `processlifecycle.DiscoverPIDByCWD(ProcessName, cwd, …)`, and the cwd it needs is available from the very first transcript line — `session.start.data.context.cwd` — which `ParseLine` then re-stamps onto every subsequent event. No sidecar read and no waiting for a turn to complete.

## Driver

`replaydata/agents/copilot/driver-interactive.sh` advertises `send`, `wait_turn` and `sleep` in `DRIVE_ELICITS`, which is the whole recipe. It launches with `--allow-all --no-color` under an isolated `COPILOT_HOME`, and dismisses the folder-trust modal by pane match (seeding `trustedFolders` alone was verified insufficient on 1.0.77). No missing primitive, so `driver=ready`.

An interactive (`script`) recipe is required rather than headless: the process must outlive the observation window for the pre-session row and the PID binding to be visible at all, and Copilot's headless mode exits at turn completion.
caveats: Lazy transcript materialization, same divergence claudecode documents: the `<session-id>` row only appears once the first prompt writes events.jsonl. The spec's 'within 1s of agent launch' bullet is satisfied by the `proc-<PID>` pre-session row. The session DIRECTORY does exist at launch, but holds only workspace.yaml, which sessionIDFromPath ignores by design.

The 1000 ms budget is anchored to the daemon's process-scan tick and is PROVISIONAL until the recording confirms it — no copilot recording exists yet, so the timing is inferred from the generic scanner path and the sibling claudecode/codex recordings, not measured for this adapter.

The `model` observation is deliberately left unpinned: this account can reach only gpt-5-mini and claude-haiku-4.5, `--model` accepts only "auto", and the auto-router picks per turn — so which model answers the nudge is not deterministic. `record` should fill it only if it proves stable.

Pre-session binding depends on `pgrep -x` matching the NATIVE copilot binary rather than the node loader that spawns it (the npm distribution is a two-process tree whose child's accounting name is "copilot"). Verified on the npm install path only; Homebrew and the install-script paths are untested, and a distribution that runs the agent under a differently-named executable would break bullet 1's pre-session row.

sources.note: Identity.Name=copilot, Source variant FilesUnderRoot{Dir: sessionsDir(), SessionIDFromPath: sessionIDFromPath}, Process.Match=ExactName{copilot}, PIDForSession=DiscoverPID.

Store layout $COPILOT_HOME/session-state/<session-id>/events.jsonl (default ~/.copilot/session-state); sessionIDFromPath accepts only the constant events.jsonl basename, so the sibling workspace.yaml present at launch cannot mint a session row.

DiscoverPID delegates to processlifecycle.DiscoverPIDByCWD(ProcessName, cwd, …) — the cwd comes from session.start.data.context.cwd, the transcript's first line, so PID binding needs no sidecar and no completed turn.

TestWatcher_EmitsSessionForNewDirectory starts the watcher, waits for Ready(), then creates <root>/<uuid>/events.jsonl — proving the production shape (session directory created at runtime, after the watcher is up) yields an event keyed by the directory name.

parseSessionStart sets ev.Skip=true while still supplying cwd and copilotVersion, so session birth settles in ready rather than tripping the classifier's transcript-activity→working default; assistant.message carries model + outputTokens, which queueOutputIncrement turns into a live token contribution.

Lines 347 and 543 mint the proc-<PID> pre-session row generically from Process.Match — the mechanism behind the 'ready + PID bound within 1s of launch' bullets is adapter-agnostic, so copilot inherits it by declaring ExactName.

DRIVE_ELICITS advertises send/wait_turn/sleep (the whole recipe); launches with --allow-all --no-color under an isolated COPILOT_HOME and dismisses the folder-trust modal by pane match, since seeding trustedFolders was verified insufficient on 1.0.77.

TestCopilotAlias_ResolvesToRealCostEstimate: both models this account can reach price non-zero (gpt-5-mini already resolved; claude-haiku-4.5 now aliased to claude-haiku-4-5), which is what makes the cost_nonzero observation safe to assert without pinning a model.

preconditions: copilot CLI on PATH and authenticated (npm i -g @github/copilot; credentials live in the OS keychain and survive COPILOT_HOME isolation)
an active Copilot plan with AI credits — the nudge turn spends them
irrlichd is recording — either run-cell.sh in isolated mode, or --attach against a running daemon started with --record
setup: Create an empty cwd under <staging>/cwd/ (the driver seeds trustedFolders in COPILOT_HOME/config.json and additionally dismisses the folder-trust modal by pane match)
Point COPILOT_HOME at <staging>/copilot-home so the session store is isolated from the maintainer's real ~/.copilot

script.text: Reply with exactly the word: ok

verify: events.jsonl contains a presession_created event for proc-<PID> within 1000 ms of the tmux new-session timestamp
events.jsonl contains a state_transition to ready for proc-<PID> within 100 ms of presession_created (pre-session is born ready)
events.jsonl contains a pid_discovered event within 1000 ms of agent launch
events.jsonl contains a transcript_new event for the <session-id> session shortly after the first send (copilot writes events.jsonl only on the first prompt)
session tokens and estimated cost are both non-zero after the turn completes
